To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a bacterial gene can be transduced into a mammalian cell, the transduced gene can be maintained intact in the host cell, and the transduced bacterial gene can be recovered in its original form by cleavage of the cell's DNA with restriction endonucleasesthat cleave only at the bacterial DNA segment.
a bacterial gene can be transduced into mammalian cells by a hybrid viral genome.
a bacterial gene was transduced into a mammalian cell and was recovered intact from the cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transduction of a bacterial suppressor tRNA into mammalian cells and its effect on the host cell.

the development of a general method for introducing bacterial genes into mammalian cells, the study of the fate of the hybrid genome in transformed and persistently infected cell lines, and the analysis of the mechanism(s) of gene expression in these systems.
the use of a bacterial DNA segment to study the fate of foreign DNA in mammalian cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the bacterial DNA segment, su+ III, has been transduced into the mammalian cell genome.
the SV40-su III chimera was not integrated into the genome of the host cells, and that the bacterial DNA was recovered intact.
a foreign gene has been introduced into mammalian cells by transduction and that the gene is expressed and maintained as an extrachromosomal element in these cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to transduce a bacterial gene into a mammalian cell and have it persist in the cell line.

the su+III gene was not expressed in either cell line, and the SV40-su +III hybrid genome did not integrate into the cellular genome of the transformed rat embryo cells or the persistently infected monkey kidney cells.
the SV40-suIII chimera was able to replicate in the absence of SV40 early gene function and was able to transform cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bacterial DNA segment is present in the mammalian cells as a discrete entity and is not extensively modified or rearranged.
the bacterial DNA segment is not lost during the replication of the hybrid genome.
the bacterial su+III gene can be stably introduced into the mammalian cells and is expressed in the transformed rat embryo cells but not in the persistently infected monkey kidney cells.
